drivers.name: APC Switched Rack PDU
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls APC Switched Rack PDUs over SNMP v2c. Outlets, banks, phases and the temperature/humidity sensor are addressable children read off the device, with named on/off/reboot commands, per-outlet delays, load thresholds and energy metering. Covers both the Rack PDU 2G MIB (AP84xx/86xx/88xx/89xx) and the first-generation one (AP79xx), detected on connect.

help.overview: APC Switched Rack PDUs are the metered power strips in most equipment racks. Each outlet is a child entity here, so a macro, schedule or panel button can switch one outlet, reboot a wedged device, or bring the whole rack up in sequence using the delays configured on the PDU itself. Bank and phase load, the breaker rating and the rack temperature sensor come through as live values you can alert on.
help.setup:
1. Give the Rack PDU's Network Management Card an IP address and reach its web interface.
2. Under Configuration > Network > SNMPv1, enable SNMPv1 access and note the community strings. Switching outlets needs a community with Write access — APC ships that as 'private' on Access Control entry 2, and its Access Type must be Write or Write+ for a command to be accepted.
3. Restrict the write community's NMS IP to the OpenAVC server's address, not 0.0.0.0, so only this server can switch outlets.
4. Enter the PDU's IP and both community strings here, then run Test Connection — it reads the PDU's own model and serial back, which proves the address and the read community, and reports which MIB branch the unit answered on.
5. Outlets appear as children once connected. If the count is wrong, use Refresh from Device.

compatible_models.notes: Rack PDU 2G and later, on the rPDU2 MIB branch. Switched models expose outlet control; Switched Metered-by-Outlet models (AP89xx) add per-outlet current, power and energy. Metered-only models connect and report banks, phases and device load with no outlet switching. The outlet, bank, phase and sensor rosters are read off the device, so a 16-outlet and a 24-outlet unit each surface exactly what they have.

First-generation Switched Rack PDUs, on the legacy rPDU MIB branch, detected automatically. Outlet switching, per-outlet delays and naming, phase current and bank load state all work. No per-outlet metering, no device energy meter and no sensor port on this generation, so those values stay blank.

drivers.name: Middle Atlantic RackLink PDU
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Middle Atlantic / Legrand RackLink RLNK power distribution units (Select, Premium, Premium+) over the RackLink Control Protocol on TCP port 60000. Outlet and dry-contact control, sequencing, naming, EPO, and live voltage / current / temperature / wattage telemetry. Premium models push unsolicited status changes; Select models fall back to polling.

help.overview: RackLink is the Middle Atlantic (now Legrand AV) family of network-controlled rack PDUs commonly installed in commercial AV racks. The driver speaks the binary RackLink Control Protocol so macros can switch outlets on / off, cycle outlets to power-cycle frozen gear, sequence the rack up / down, and (on Premium / Premium+ units) read live telemetry.
help.setup:
1. Connect the PDU to your network via Ethernet.
2. Find the PDU's IP from the RackLink front panel or web UI.
3. Log into the PDU's web UI as Administrator and set the passwords for Administrator, User, and Control Systems accounts. The control protocol is disabled until those passwords are set.
4. On Premium+ models, enable the control protocol under Device Settings → Network Services → Control Protocol, and enter a username for an admin account that has the control protocol enabled.
5. Enter the IP, port 60000, and credentials in the device config in OpenAVC. Default Select / Premium credentials are user / password (whatever was set in step 3).

compatible_models.notes: All RackLink series share the Control Protocol on TCP 60000. Select models support outlet control, naming, sequencing, and dry contacts. Premium and Premium+ add per-system telemetry (voltage, current, wattage, temperature, surge state, occupancy), EPO, and pushed status updates.

drivers.name: NETIO PowerPDU, PowerBOX, PowerCable and PowerDIN
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls NETIO rack PDUs, smart power strips, power cables and DIN-rail units over the unit's web login (firmware 5.1.3 and later) or NETIO's JSON API: switch each output on or off, toggle it, reboot it or turn it on for a set time, and read each output's load, current, power factor and energy on metered models. Digital inputs, NETIO temperature and humidity sensors, each output's schedule and the unit's own watchdogs, rules and power analysis blocks are reported as live values. Over the web login the unit's firmware can be checked and updated from NETIO's update server and the unit restarted; on OpenAVC 0.37.2 and later, its HTTPS certificate installed, firmware installed from a file, and its configuration backed up and restored.

help.overview: NETIO makes networked rack PDUs, power strips, power cables and DIN-rail units. Each output is a child entity here, so a macro, schedule or panel button can switch one output, reboot a frozen device, or switch an output on for a set time. On metered models each output's load and energy are reported too. Connected with the web login, an output switching shows the moment it happens and each output's schedule is reported, the unit's firmware can be checked and updated from NETIO's update server, and the unit can be restarted. On OpenAVC 0.37.2 and later Send Command also installs an HTTPS certificate, installs firmware from a file, and backs up and restores the unit's configuration. The results of the unit's own IP watchdogs, rules and power analysis blocks are reported with the JSON API only.
help.setup:
1. Choose Connect With. The web login (firmware 5.1.3 and later) needs nothing turned on: enter a user from the NETIO's web interface as Username and Password. A user allowed to control outputs can switch them. Renaming an output, turning its schedule on or off and resetting its energy counter need a user that may change output settings. Checking for and installing firmware updates, restarting the unit, its HTTPS certificate and backing up or restoring its configuration need a user that may change the unit's settings, such as an administrator.
2. For the JSON API instead, open M2M API Protocols in the NETIO's web interface, then the JSON API tab. Turn on Enable JSON API, Enable READ-ONLY and Enable WRITE, and save. The unit restarts its web server, so it answers errors for a few seconds. The tab has a username and password for reading and another pair for writing; NETIO ships both as netio / netio. Enter the reading login as Username and Password here, and the writing login under Advanced only when it is different.
3. Port: for the web login, the port the web interface answers on (80, or 443 with Use HTTPS on); for the JSON API, the port on its tab (80 unless it was changed). The JSON API serves HTTPS from firmware 5.0.3, but slowly: the NETIO takes about 4 seconds to open each secure connection and the JSON API opens one per request, so with HTTPS on, use the web login.
4. Outputs, inputs, watchdogs, rules and power analysis blocks appear as children once connected.

compatible_models.notes: Tested on a unit on firmware 5.2.4 and 5.3.2, over both the web login and the JSON API, HTTP and HTTPS: every command, metering with a load plugged in, a NETIO temperature and humidity sensor, outputs switched from elsewhere showing at once over the web login, and the full firmware update from 5.2.4 to 5.3.2. Over HTTPS the JSON API answers each request in about 4 seconds; the web login is quick. Resetting an output's energy counter over the JSON API needs firmware 5.3; on 5.2.4 use the web login. Turning an output's schedule on or off needs a schedule assigned to it in the NETIO's web interface. The first firmware check after the NETIO starts sometimes gets no answer from NETIO's server; the driver asks once more.

Run against NETIO's public demo units on firmware 5.3.1 and 5.3.2. JSON API: identity, outputs, inputs, metering, watchdogs, rules and power analysis blocks read; outputs switched, toggled, rebooted, switched on for a time and renamed. Web login: the same reads, each output's schedule, and the outputs' switching pushed as it happened; outputs switched, toggled, rebooted and switched on for a time (the demo login may not rename outputs, change their schedules or reset energy counters, so those were not run over the web login). The firmware, certificate, configuration and restart commands were not run on these units: the demo login may not change settings.

Same universal firmware, JSON API and web login as the units above; the outlet type in the model name (S, B, F, E, G, Z) does not change the API. Metering follows the model: K models meter every output, Q models the whole unit and output 1, P models switch without metering. Firmware 5.4 reads its outputs' states from a topic of its own over the web login; that path follows NETIO's library and has not been run on a 5.4 unit.

tcp_probe.send_ascii:
GET /emweb HTTP/1.1
Host: netio
Upgrade: websocket
Connection: Upgrade
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13

drivers.name: WattBox IP-Controlled PDU
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls SnapAV WattBox IP-controlled power distribution units over the WattBox Integration Protocol (Telnet, port 23). Outlets are addressable children with per-outlet state, name, and power metering. Supports on/off/toggle/reset, per-outlet naming, auto-reboot configuration, system + per-outlet power metering, and UPS status reporting on units with a connected UPS.

help.overview: WattBox is the SnapAV / Snap One family of IP-controlled power distribution units commonly installed in commercial AV racks. This driver speaks the v1.7 Integration Protocol, letting macros switch outlets on / off / reset, rename outlets, configure auto-reboot, and read live power / UPS telemetry. Use this driver instead of OvrC for local OpenAVC control — OvrC is a separate cloud product.
help.setup:
1. Connect the WattBox to your network via Ethernet.
2. Find the WattBox's IP from the front panel (where applicable) or from the WattBox web interface.
3. In the WattBox web interface, ensure the integration protocol is enabled and confirm the admin username and password.
4. Enter the IP, port 23, and credentials in the device config in OpenAVC.
5. Outlets are 1-indexed in commands. Use Reset All Outlets to power-cycle the whole unit.

compatible_models.notes: All current IP / IPV / IPVM WattBoxes share the v1.7 Integration Protocol. Outlets are reconciled from the unit's reported outlet count, so 3 / 12 / 18-outlet models each surface exactly their outlets as children.
